goal: This is a production HEP reconstruction codebase: OMILREC v1.0.0, the maximum-likelihood vertex/energy reconstruction algorithm of a JUNO-like liquid-scintillator detector. The production algorithm lives in OMILRECV2/src/ (C++; the frozen CMake config builds it against the JUNO software stack, which is mounted at /cvmfs). Your job: make it faster — drive SPEED_MS down (single-threaded mean milliseconds per event over the 100-event benchmark; see scripts/sl_eval_v100.sh) — while every frozen correctness gate stays PASS. The gates probe the production Calculate_EVLikelihood itself (CONTRACT), hold the likelihood to a relative error below 1e-13 on 4 events x 4 Minuit stages against frozen golden points (FCN), hold the 18-event end-to-end reconstruction within 4 mm / 7 keV / 10 ps / 0.1 PE of the frozen reference (CONSISTENCY), and pin every thread source to 1 — a speedup must come from the algorithm, not parallelism (SINGLE_THREADED). The editable surface is OMILRECV2/src only; tests/, scripts/, baseline/ and the build configuration are fixed. The frozen v1.0.0 baseline is SPEED_MS 919.9 on this machine (baseline/manifest.json; the eval also reports SPEEDUP_V100 against it). The research target is SPEED_MS at or below 170 ms/evt — about 5.4x the baseline; lower is always better at every step, and progress short of the target still counts. A full eval is heavyweight — two cmake builds, three pytest gate suites, then the benchmark, on the order of 5-8 minutes. repo docs (README.md, docs/RUN.md, CLAUDE.md) describe the build and gate flow.
gate_block:
Only modify files under OMILRECV2/src/. The harness runs, in order:
  - bash scripts/sl_eval_v100.sh --evtmax 100
It builds with ENABLE_FCN_GATE_PROBE=ON, runs the CONTRACT / FCN / CONSISTENCY gate suites, rebuilds probe-free, then benchmarks the production library (single-threaded) and emits SPEED_MS (ms/evt, lower is better) plus the four gate tokens. A change is accepted only if CONTRACT=FCN=CONSISTENCY=SINGLE_THREADED=PASS; among accepted changes, lower SPEED_MS is better.;

Measured on this machine, for planning: the same script with a smaller --evtmax is a probe — roughly tens of seconds at 10 events versus minutes for the full 100-event evaluation including its two builds — and its gates are a subset of the full ones (in this bit-exact task the FCN points are 4 events). Three repeats of the frozen baseline spread 895.6-921.5 ms/evt (~±1.5%): treat smaller deltas as ties until your own repeats of a fixed state say otherwise.
